SPECIFICATION FOR WATER BASED RECORDER
0. FOREWORD

INKS

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 13 December 1976, after the draft finalized by the Inks and Allied Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council.
0.2 Recorder inks are used with automatic instrument recorders, in which a trace is drawn on a moving sheet of paper. Since the quality of a record depends on the paper as well as on the ink, it is necessary to use paper of the right quality. The specification for paper is covered under IS : 5947-1970*. 0.3 For the purpose of deciding whether standard is complied with, the final expressing the result of a test or analysis, ance with IS : Z-1960?. The number of rounded off value should be the same as standard. a particular requirement of this value, observed or calculated, shall be rounded off in accordsignificant places retained in the that of the specified value in this

SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampling and test for water based inks used in automatic single point and multipoint instrument recorders for marking permanent continuous/ intermittent trace on a sheet 13~ long roll of paper. 1.1.1 It does not cover inks for use with recorders dot marks are used. 2. IS : 8277 - 1976 5.2.1 Reference ink for slow drying type shall be made by dissolving 10 g of the appropriate dye specified in 5.2 in 1000 ml of a mixture of equal volumes of glycerine ( glycerol ) and distilled water ( see IS : 10701960* ). Reference ink for quick drying type shall be made by dissolving the same quantity of dye in 1000 ml of a mixture of one volume of glycerine ( glycerol ) and three volumes of distilled water. 5.3 Marking in A-I. QUALITY

6.1 The ink shall continue to satisfy the requirements prescribed in 5 for a minimum period of 24 months from the date of packing when stored in air-tight containers and kept at ambient room temperature. 7. PACKING 7.1 Packing AND MARKING

7.1.1 The ink shall be packed in suitable glass or plastics containers of 25, 50 and 100 ml capacity or of 500 ml capacity, if desired. 7.1.2 The containers shall be closed plastics screw caps such-that when tilted out of the bottle. tightly with leak-proof cork or or shaken no trace of ink flows

7.1.3 Each container shall be accompanied by a suitable small ink dropper with which the marking instrument or ink reservoir can be filled conveniently. 7.1.4 Ten each of the 25- , 50. or lOO-ml containers cardboard carton provided with suitable partitions. shall be separately packed in a cardboard carton. 7.2 Marking label containing a) b) c) d) Each container and cardboard the following information: shall be packed in a Each 500-ml bottle shall have a neat

NOTE-The use of the IS1 Certification Mark in governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution (Certification Marks ) Act and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The IS1 Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by IS1 and operated by the producer. IS1 marked products are also continuously checked by IS1 for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the IS1 Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.

8.1 The method

APPENDIX A ( CZauses 5.3 to 5.6 )
METHODS A-1; TEST A-l.1 OF TEST FOR WATER QUALITY BASED RECORDER INKS

FOR MARKING

Procedure - Before the test, the ink reservoir of the recorder shall be properly washed with spirit or water and the marking instrument shall be cleaned with spirit to remove grease. The reservoir shall be filled with the reference ink ( see 5.2.1) and the sample ink at least twice and emptied. The test shall be carried out on the same chart for recording meteorological instruments ( see IS : 5947-1970*~) at about the same temperature. A-1.1.1 With the reservoir filled with the ink, continuausly write about ten lines on the chart paper. The marking instrument pressure on the paper shall be normal and the width or the marking point shall not The ink shall be considered to have passed the test if it exceed O-5 mm. satisfies the following conditions:
a) During the writing stylus as indicated there is no excessive flow of the ink from by drops or smudges; ink match those with the the

b) The lines drawn with the sample reference ink visually in all respects;

*Specification for charts for recording meteorological instruments.

IS: 8277 - 1976 After one hour in case of slow drying ink, and 10 to 50 seconds in case of quick drying ink, when a blotting paper is placed on the test paper no impression is transferred on to the blotting paper; The ink retains the flow after 24 hours from the time of filling; and If the tip is kept on the chart stationary for 24 hours, the ink On restarting the chart drive the shall not smudge on the chart, ink flow shall be maintained automatically. A-2. TEST FOR PERMANENCE A-2.1 Daylight Exposure

A-2.1.1 Proczdure -Dry the stripe obtained in A-l.1 for 15 minutes. Cut the paper into strips, each 5 cm wide and at right angles to the marking. Expose the markings for 8 days to air and diffused daylight in the shade. At the same time and under the same conditions, perform the experiment with the reference ink (see 5.2.1 ). A-2.1.1.1 The markings of the ink shall show a close match to those of the reference ink. A-2.2 Ultra-Violet Ray Exposure

A-2.2.1 Procedure - Place the papers containing the markings from ink and the reference ink at a distance of 25 cm from an ultra-violet lamp ( see A-2.2.1.1 ) normal to the rays, and expose for a total period of 36 h. A-2.2.1.1 The ultra-vio:et UV region chiefly at 3 655 A. lamp shall be of 125 W and of long wave

A-2.2.1.2 The darkness ( intensity ) of the markings from the ink shall be at least equal to that of the markings from the reference ink, A-3. TEST A-3.1 FOR STABILITY

Apparatus
Glass Beaker -

A-3.1.1

unlipped, 100 ml capacity.

A-3.2 Procedure - Take 50 ml of the ink in an unlipped beaker of 100 ml capacity. Mark the level of the liquid, cover it with a watch glass and leave for 15 days in a place uncontaminated by dust and chemical fumes. Examine for moulds and flakes after this period, A-3.2.1 Make up the volume with water and stir. Allow to stand for 24 hours and filter, The ink shall remain non-gelatinous and shall leave no residue on filtration. 7

IS : 8277 - 1976 A-4. TEST FOR HOMOGENEITY

-A-4.1 Procedure

-Shake the ink thoroughly. Withdraw 10 ml and transfer to a clean centrifuge tube. Centrifuge for 2 minutes at 1 500 rev/ min. Remove the tube carefully without shaking and decant the liquid slowly. A-4.1.1 The ink shall be considered no sediment found in the tube. to have passed the test if there is

APPENDIX ( Clause 8.1 )
SAMPLING B-l. GENERAL OF WATER REQUIREMENTS BASED

B
RECORDER INKS

OF SAMPLING the

B-1.0 In drawing, preparing, storing and handling test samples precautions and directions given in B-l.1 to B-l.4 shall be observed. B-l.1 Samples shall be drawn from original unopened bottles. B-L.2 Samples shall not be taken in an exposed place.

B-l.3 Unless otherwise stated in any test method, sample ink from each of the selected bottles shall be drawn after shaking and then allowing the fluid to come to rest. B-l.4 Each of the sample containers shall be marked with full details sampling and the month and year of the manufacture of the material. B-2. SCALE OF SAMPLING of

B-2.1 All the bottles in a single consignment of the material containing ink of the same type and colour shall be grouped together to form a lot. B-2.2 Samples of the ink shall be tested from each lot separately for ascertaining the conformity of the material to the requirements of the specification. B-2.3 The number of bottles (n) to be chosen from the lot (.7V) depends upon the size of the lot and shall be in accordance with Table 1. B-2.4 These bottles shall be chosen at random from the lot. In order to ensure randomness of selection some random number table may be used. For guidance to random selection procedures, reference may be made to IS : 4905-1968*.
*Methods for random sampling.
